name: Postaxial Tetramelic Oligodactyly

criteria.description: Presence of postaxial oligodactyly affecting all four limbs
Sparing of preaxial digits (thumbs) with normal development
Radiographic evidence of absent or hypoplastic postaxial digits in all limbs
Positive family history of similar limb malformations
No associated major visceral or neurological anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of postaxial oligodactyly in all four limbs confirmed clinically and radiographically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be inconclusive.

imaging: Radiographs showing absent or hypoplastic postaxial digits in all four limbs
Shortened metacarpals and metatarsals of affected digits
Hypoplasia of carpal and tarsal bones
genetic: No consistent causative gene identified; sporadic and familial cases reported
other: Clinical examination revealing symmetrical postaxial oligodactyly

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of extra postaxial digits rather than missing digits
Often associated with syndactyly and polydactyly
Central ray deficiency with median clefts of hands and feet

redFlags: Presence of associated visceral or neurological anomalies
Progressive limb deformities beyond congenital presentation
Severe functional impairment of hands or feet
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) - Limb Malformations
